locator: I q.5 a.1 co.: Intantum est autem perfectum unumquodque, inquantum est actu
interpretation: Third step: each thing is perfect insofar as it is in act. Read per perfection as a biconditional: perfect in a perfection exactly when actually having it. The article's following clause ('esse enim est actualitas omnis rei, ut ex superioribus patet') carries the conclusion from act to being; it is not part of this statement and is not used by the derivation, because STMT-GOODNESS-IS-ACTUALITY stops at act. Ad 1 distinguishes perfect simpliciter (ultimate perfection) from perfect secundum quid; the statement is about perfection in one respect.
